title: Signed first-variable shift compatibility of the internal-Hom line comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use its unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ordinary derived tensor $\otimes_R^L$, namely the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after K-flat replacement of the first factor [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $H(A,B)=R\mathcal Hom_R(A,B)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with the derived tensor--internal-Hom adjunction and signed shift identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; transposes below are taken for this adjunction. Let $T$ be an $R$-module sheaf locally isomorphic to $R$, placed in degree zero. Fix $r,s\in\mathbf Z$ with $r$ even, and $K\in D(R)$, without a boundedness or perfectness hypothesis. Define
$$
a_{K,T[r]}:H(K,R)\otimes_R^L T[r]\longrightarrow H(K,T[r])
$$
to be the transpose of coefficient evaluation tensored with $1_{T[r]}$; define $a_{K[s],T[r]}$ in the same way. Under the cohomological shift conventions $C[s]^i=C^{i+s}$ and $d_{C[s]}=(-1)^s d_C$, let $b_{K,B,s}:H(K[s],B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K,B)[-s]$ be the first-variable shift identification. Then the square from $H(K[s],R)\otimes^L T[r]$ to $H(K,T[r])[-s]$ commutes:
$$
b_{K,T[r],s}\circ a_{K[s],T[r]}
=a_{K,T[r]}[-s]\circ\bigl(b_{K,R,s}\otimes1_{T[r]}\bigr),
$$
where on the right one inserts the usual tensor-shift isomorphism $H(K,R)[-s]\otimes^L T[r]\cong(H(K,R)\otimes^L T[r])[-s]$. The maps are those of the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] and total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. On Hom-complex representatives the first-variable comparison reindexes $j=i+s$ and has degree-$n$ multiplier $(-1)^{sn}$; using any coherent normalization differing by a sign depending only on $s$ gives the same commuting square.

proof.text:
Choose K-flat representatives for the tensor input and a K-injective representative for the Hom target, using the derived constructions in the statement. The ordinary tensor is the total tensor complex, with the Koszul sign $(-1)^p$ on the second differential, and the internal Hom is the product Hom complex with differential $d(f)=d_Bf-(-1)^n f d_A$. The transpose defining $a_{K,T[r]}$ is therefore represented by the usual chain-level tensor--Hom evaluation transpose; the same description applies after replacing $K$ by $K[s]$. The K-flat and K-injective replacement choices compute the stated derived functors and do not alter the resulting morphisms in $D(R)$.

The cited definitions give exactly the complexes and replacement procedure used here.

proof.text: For a homogeneous degree-$n$ family $f=(f^i)_i$ representing a morphism from $K[s]$ to the target, the first-variable shift comparison is the reindexing $j=i+s$ with component multiplier $(-1)^{sn}$. Substituting this formula into the differential displayed in the Hom-complex definition gives a chain map to $H(K,B)[-s]$; the two signs from the shifted source differential cancel the sign change in the Hom differential. Thus this is precisely the map $b_{K,B,s}$, and it is natural in the target $B$, including the map induced by any morphism $B	o B'$.

source.place: Section 0A8X: Hom-complex differential; signed first-variable shift formula supplied by literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-six-functors/sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect/thm-sf-dual-perfect.proof.md Step 4 (agent expansion)

proof.text: Evaluate both composites in the asserted square on a homogeneous tensor $f\otimes t$, where $f$ has Hom degree $n$ and $t$ lies in the shifted line $T[r]$. The right-hand route first contributes $(-1)^{sn}$ from $b_{K,R,s}$ and then applies the evaluation transpose. The left-hand route applies the transpose into $T[r]$ first, so the same reindexing is taken in target degree $n+r$ and contributes $(-1)^{s(n+r)}$. The tensor totalization contributes the same Koszul sign to both routes. Their ratio is $(-1)^{s(n+r)-sn}=(-1)^{sr}=1$ because $r$ is even. Hence the two composites agree on every homogeneous tensor and therefore as maps of total complexes. This calculation also shows that multiplying every $b_{K,B,s}$ by a normalization sign depending only on $s$ leaves the square unchanged, since that factor occurs once on each path.

proof.text: The chain-level equality is natural in representatives and in the morphism of the second Hom variable. The derived internal Hom is well defined after changing representatives, while the ringed-site internal-Hom theorem supplies the natural shift identifications and their compatibility with morphisms. Therefore the equality descends through localization to the displayed morphism equality in $D(R)$ for arbitrary $K$ and all integers $s$, with only the stated parity condition on $r$.
